prompt:
A circuit has two resistors in series, $R_1={{R1}}\ \Omega$ and $R_2={{R2}}\ \Omega$, connected to a ${{V}}\text{ V}$ battery.

Find the equivalent resistance, the circuit current, and the voltage drop across each resistor. Use $R_{eq}=R_1+R_2$, $V=IR$, and explain why $V_1+V_2$ should equal the battery voltage.
teacher_notes: Longer equation-heavy FR item for section timing and response space.
explanation: $R_{eq}={{R1}}+{{R2}}={{calc: R1 + R2}}\ \Omega$. The current is $I=\frac{V}{R_{eq}}=\frac{{{V}}}{{{calc: R1 + R2}}}={{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}}\text{ A}$. $V_1=IR_1=({{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}})({{R1}})={{calc: round(V * R1 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$ and $V_2=IR_2=({{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}})({{R2}})={{calc: round(V * R2 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$. The drops add to ${{V}}\text{ V}$, matching the battery.

rubric.criterion: Finds total current using Ohm's law
Explains voltage conservation around the loop

sample_solution: $R_{eq}={{calc: R1 + R2}}\ \Omega$, so $I={{V}}\text{ V}/{{calc: R1 + R2}}\ \Omega={{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}}\text{ A}$. Then $V_1={{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}}({{R1}})={{calc: round(V * R1 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$ and $V_2={{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}}({{R2}})={{calc: round(V * R2 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$.
exemplar_answer: The two resistors are in series, so their resistances add to ${{calc: R1 + R2}}\ \Omega$. The same current flows through both resistors, giving $I={{calc: round(V / (R1 + R2), 2)}}\text{ A}$. The voltage drops are ${{calc: round(V * R1 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$ and ${{calc: round(V * R2 / (R1 + R2), 1)}}\text{ V}$, and these add to ${{V}}\text{ V}$ because the battery energy per charge is used across the two resistors.
